summary: We are allowed to repair exactly one broken lamp, so we try every broken lamp and keep the best result (T6 — try every option). For a repaired lamp, the lit stretch is: lit lamps on its left + 1 (itself) + lit lamps on its right.

blocks.title: Read the lamps as text
blocks.text: Keep the row as a **string** like `'0011'`. `int()` would turn it into `11` and silently delete the broken lamps at the front. `.strip()` removes stray spaces around the input so they are not counted as lamps.

blocks.title: Remember the length and the best so far
blocks.text: `n` is used by the right-hand walk to know where the row ends. `best` starts at 0 and is raised by every repair we try.

blocks.title: Try repairing each broken lamp
blocks.text: We visit every position, but only a `'0'` can be repaired, so the `if` skips lit lamps. Inside the `if` we pretend lamp `i` is fixed and measure how long the lit stretch becomes.

blocks.title: Count lit lamps to the left
blocks.text: Start just left of the repaired lamp (`j = i - 1`) and step left while lamps are lit. The `j >= 0` check must come **first**: without it, `j` reaches -1 and `lamps[-1]` silently reads the LAST lamp, so lamps from the far end get counted. Because `and` stops early, `lamps[j]` is never read once `j` is out of range.

blocks.title: Count lit lamps to the right
blocks.text: The same walk going right from `i + 1`. Here `j < n` stops us at the end of the row — without it the program would crash with `IndexError`.

blocks.title: Score this repair and keep the best
blocks.text: The new stretch is `left + 1 + right`: the `+ 1` is the lamp we just fixed. Forgetting it makes every answer one too small. `max` keeps the best repair seen so far.

complexity: Time O(N²) in the worst case with N ≤ 100 → about 10,000 steps, instant.
pitfalls: `int(input())` destroys leading zeros — keep it a string.
No `j >= 0` check → `lamps[-1]` wraps around to the last lamp.
Forgetting the `+ 1` for the repaired lamp.
